prompt.context: Our client is a major airline company. The CEO has contacted us (a BCG partner) because he wants to put one more passenger on each of his company's flights. We are about to go into a meeting with him and need to prepare two things: (1) the financial return of adding one more passenger per flight and whether it is worthwhile, and (2) the marketing strategy to attract these new passengers.
prompt.question: Before the meeting: (1) Estimate the financial return of putting one more passenger on each flight. Is it worthwhile? (2) What marketing strategy would you recommend to attract these new passengers?

clarifying_info.q: Does the airline have enough capacity (empty seats) to accommodate one more passenger per flight?
clarifying_info.a: Yes, you can assume there is enough capacity to put one more passenger onboard.

clarifying_info.q: What routes does the airline operate and what are the ticket prices?
clarifying_info.a: The airline operates in the Brazilian domestic market only. 60% of flights are between Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro (45 minutes, ticket price US$100). 20% are between other major capitals (1.5 hours apart, ticket price US$100). 20% are between other cities (3 hours apart, ticket price US$300).

clarifying_info.q: How many airplanes does the company have?
clarifying_info.a: The company has 100 airplanes available (the company actually has a little under 10% more but roughly 10% are in maintenance at any given time, so 100 are available).

clarifying_info.q: What share of planes fly short vs. long routes?
clarifying_info.a: You can assume 80% of planes fly the 1-hour routes and 20% fly the 3-hour routes.

framework: Revenue side: estimate average ticket price across route mix, then estimate total new passengers (= number of flights per day x days per month)
Cost side: assess marginal cost of one additional passenger — variable cost per incremental passenger is negligible (food, fuel negligible at margin), so marginal cost ≈ 0
Profit impact: incremental profit ≈ incremental revenue
Marketing strategy: identify which customer segments have capacity to fill the empty seat and what levers (pricing, loyalty, channels, partnerships) attract them

questions.prompt: Calculate the average ticket price across the airline's route mix.
questions.guidance: Weight each route by its share of flights: 80% of flights cost $100 (SP-Rio 60% + other capitals 20%) and 20% cost $300. Average = (0.80 × $100) + (0.20 × $300) = $80 + $60 = $140.

math.setup: Route mix: 80% of flights at $100, 20% of flights at $300. Weighted average ticket price = (80% × $100) + (20% × $300).

questions.prompt: Estimate the total number of flights per day operated by the airline.
questions.guidance: Start with 100 available planes. Split 80 planes on 1-hour routes and 20 planes on 3-hour routes. Define operating hours: first flight departs 6 am, last flight arrives midnight = 18 operating hours. Ground time between flights = ~1 hour (taxi 10 min + deplane 15 min + clean/resupply 10 min + board 15 min + taxi 10 min = 60 min). Short route cycle = 1h flight + 1h ground = 2h → 18/2 = 9 flights/plane/day. Long route cycle = 3h flight + 1h ground = 4h → 18/4 ≈ 4 flights/plane/day. Total = 80×9 + 20×4 = 720 + 80 = 800 flights/day.

math.setup: Operating window: 6 am to midnight = 18 hours. Ground turnaround = 60 minutes. Short-haul cycle = 1h + 1h = 2h; long-haul cycle = 3h + 1h = 4h.
steps: Short flights per plane per day: 18h / 2h = 9
Long flights per plane per day: 18h / 4h ≈ 4

questions.prompt: Calculate the incremental monthly revenue (and profit) from adding one passenger per flight.
questions.guidance: One extra passenger per flight means 800 new passengers per day. Revenue per new passenger = average ticket price = $140. Monthly revenue = 800 × 30 × $140 = $3,360,000. The marginal cost of one additional passenger is negligible (small food/beverage cost, negligible fuel), so marginal cost ≈ $0 and incremental profit ≈ incremental revenue.

math.setup: 800 new passengers/day × 30 days/month × $140 average ticket price.
math.answer: Incremental monthly revenue ≈ $3,360,000; incremental profit ≈ $3,360,000 (marginal cost negligible)

questions.prompt: Why is it important to estimate the financial impact before the client meeting?
questions.guidance: Having a rough order-of-magnitude estimate before the meeting gives the consulting team a sense of the size of the client's opportunity. It allows the team to frame the discussion, prioritize efforts, and arrive credible and prepared rather than discovering the numbers for the first time in front of the client.

brainstorming.prompt: What marketing strategies could the airline use to attract one additional passenger per flight?

categories.name: Pricing & Promotions
ideas: Last-minute discount fares to fill empty seats
Dynamic pricing to lower prices during off-peak times
Bundle offers (flight + hotel, flight + car rental)
Promotional fares for specific routes with low load factors

categories.name: Loyalty & Retention
ideas: Frequent flyer program enhancements to incentivize repeat booking
Upgrade vouchers or bonus miles for flexible travelers
Corporate account deals to lock in business travelers

categories.name: Distribution & Channels
ideas: Partnerships with online travel agencies (OTAs) to increase visibility
Direct website/app promotions with exclusive web-only fares
Partnerships with credit card companies for co-branded offers

categories.name: New Customer Segments
ideas: Target leisure travelers with weekend getaway packages
Attract price-sensitive students with youth fares
Target underserved secondary-city routes with introductory pricing

categories.name: Operational / Scheduling
ideas: Add more convenient departure times to attract business travelers
Code-share agreements with other carriers to feed passengers onto domestic legs
Improve on-time performance and customer experience to drive word-of-mouth

recommendation: Proceed with the initiative: adding one passenger per flight generates approximately $3.36 million in incremental monthly profit at near-zero marginal cost, making it highly attractive.
Prioritize a dynamic pricing / last-minute discount strategy to fill the marginal seat, starting with the highest-frequency SP–Rio route which represents 60% of flights.
risks: Discounting to fill the last seat could dilute revenue if not properly fenced (customers who would have paid full fare buying discounted seats instead)
Operational execution risk: ensuring consistent load-factor tracking and dynamic pricing capability requires investment in revenue management systems
next_steps: Validate actual load factors by route to identify where the empty seat opportunity is largest
Assess existing revenue management system capability for dynamic pricing
Pilot a last-minute discount program on the SP–Rio corridor and measure incremental revenue vs. cannibalization
